method: Pixel geometry only, with no encoding. The inset's target width is the frame width times the size percentage. Even alignment rounds that width down to the nearest even number (never below 2 px) and rounds the height the same way; nearest-pixel alignment rounds half up. The height is the final width divided by the inset aspect ratio, so the inset keeps the source's shape and only pixel rounding can change the fitted aspect. The margin is the frame width times the margin percentage rounded half up, and the inset is anchored to the chosen corner with that margin on the two edges it touches, which fixes its top-left corner and therefore its overlay coordinates. A layout that cannot fit — a negative corner, or an inset plus its margins wider or taller than the frame — is reported as an error instead of being clipped. The safe check compares the inset rectangle with the legacy 90% title-safe box, whose edges are 5% of the frame width from the sides and 5% of the frame height from the top and bottom; the layout is safe only when all four inset edges stay inside that box, so a 5% margin is safe on a 16:9 frame but not on a tall vertical one. Width share, area share and the fitted aspect ratio expose rounding drift, and the FFmpeg line scales the inset to the computed pixel size and overlays it at the computed corner. The model assumes square pixels, one inset and a static position; it does not scale the main video, animate the inset, model platform interface overlays, avoid faces or subtitles, or render anything. Inputs are limited to frames of 64-16384 px, inset sizes of 5-95%, margins of 0-20% and aspect ratios of 0.1-10. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: FFmpeg overlay filter documentation: x and y place the top-left of the overlaid input inside the main frame, and scale sets the overlay's pixel size.
Legacy broadcast graphics safe-area practice: a 90% title-safe box leaves a 5% border on every edge of the frame.
4:2:0 chroma subsampling and most video encoders require even frame dimensions, so odd sizes are padded or rejected.
